nodes.title: [Bug]: linux-x64 main process dies with SIGTRAP via out-of-range std::string_view::substr (hardened libc++ → LogMessage::HandleFatal → IMMEDIATE_CRASH) — Electron 41.0.3
nodes.body:
### Electron Version

41.0.3 (linux-x64; stock release binary, GNU build ID `bb7c19abf4fef1dba088a8a3595b42c17e188af8`). Current 41.x line is 41.10.7 / Chromium 146.0.7680.216 — unknown whether this is already fixed there.

### Operating System

Arch Linux (Omarchy), kernel 7.2.5 x64, Wayland (Hyprland), AMD Granite Ridge iGPU + mesa 26.2.2. Host: 30GiB RAM, no memory pressure at crash times.

### Last Known Working Electron Version

Unknown — crashes began with an app whose bundled runtime is 41.0.3; we could not A/B other Electron versions.

### What happened

A production Electron app's **main process dies instantly with SIGTRAP (`si_code=SI_KERNEL`)** — no dialog, no JS exception, nothing in the app log. Four occurrences in 5 days on one machine, always while the app was **idle** (internal telemetry seconds before each crash: 0 running tasks, 0 leases, 1 window). Two of the four crashes happened within 4 minutes of each other (relaunch → crash after 3m19s). Not correlated with memory (no OOM, 14GiB free), CPU, or user workload.

### Analysis (symbolicated with the official `electron-v41.0.3-linux-x64-debug.zip`)

All crashes land on the **same instruction**, module-relative vaddr `0x6EDE0E4` of the `electron` binary (verified across two app releases that ship the identical runtime):

```
addr2line -e debug/electron.debug -f -C -i 0x6EDE0E4
  → logging::LogMessage::HandleFatal(...)   ./../../base/immediate_crash.h:180
addr2line -e debug/electron.debug -f -C -i 0x2ae9680
  → std::__Cr::__throw_out_of_range(char const*)   ./../../third_party/libc++/src/include/stdexcept:249
```

The trap block loads the rodata string `"string_view::substr"` and calls `__throw_out_of_range` with it before the `int3` (`IMMEDIATE_CRASH`). Chain: **`std::string_view::substr(pos, …)` called with `pos > size()`** → hardened libc++ assertion (`string_view:470`) → with exceptions disabled, funneled to `logging::LogMessage::HandleFatal` (`base/logging.cc:1009`) → `IMMEDIATE_CRASH()` (`int3`) → SIGTRAP.

I.e., a native `substr` bounds violation anywhere in the main process (Electron/Chromium/Node code or a native module) is fatal by design under Chromium's hardened libc++, and in this case it recurs on a ~daily cadence.

### Timing hint (unconfirmed)

The app performs periodic `git.refresh`-style RPCs; one completed **4.8s** and another **0.24s** before the two most recent traps — a network/hostname-adjacent path is a plausible trigger. The exact caller could not be recovered: `systemd-coredump` stored cores are truncated (~22MB) and lack the crashing thread's stack.

### What I'd like

1. A check whether an out-of-range `string_view::substr` fix landed between Chromium 146.0.7680.**80** and **.216** (or in Electron's own code between 41.0.3 and 41.10.7).
2. Pointers on which main-process subsystems call `string_view::substr` on network/hostname-derived data, if that rings a bell.

Happy to provide: the four coredump records (PIDs, timestamps, truncated cores), app-log excerpts around each crash, trap-block disassembly, and the full symbolication transcript. A reproducible test case is not yet available (caller unidentified); I can re-run capture with a full-core setup if useful.
